the presence of a NE component in a urothelial neoplasm, whether it is a small cell carcinoma or a large cell NE carcinoma, is associated with a worse prognosis compared with that of a urothellial carcinoma with no NE component.5,6 The prognostic significance of a NE component is independent of the histologic type of the urothelial component (eg, small cell carcinoma vs urothelial papilloma).

we should be able to identify a small cell carcinoma of the urinary tract by its histologic and cytological features, even if the tumor is not immunoreactive for chromogranin or synaptophysin.5,6 The histologic and cytogenetic features that we believe are sufficient to identify small cell NE carcinoma of the urinary bladder include the presence of a small cell carcinoma with organoid growth and a finely clumped pattern with inconspicuous to absent nucleoli.
